source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Thrips (ទ្រីប ឬ ថ្មងផ្ទាំក់ជ័រ, including the Western flower thrips, Frankliniella occidentalis): female thrips have a reddish-orange body color, with fringed wings; body length is about 0.9 to 1.2 mm. Thrips have a body shape resembling a tiny narrow insect with reddish coloring and 7 pairs of legs (as described in the source). Thrips feeding leaves a distinctive silvery, scarred appearance on the leaf surface from their rasping-sucking feeding style, which particularly damages young leaf tissue.

Thrips have a wing-membrane pattern typical of this order, with wing length of about 0.26 mm; both nymph and adult stages feed on the underside and topside of leaves respectively. Thrips damage leaves during the young growth stage, when a plant is still developing new leaf tissue and silk, and populations of thrips can commonly be found in the field. A single female thrips can lay up to about 100 eggs, which take about 3 to 5 days to hatch. Nymphs feed on the underside of leaves for about 4 to 10 days before pupating in the soil, taking about 15 days to become adults.

Under cooler conditions, or with 2 to 5 days between generations, populations can build up rapidly. Thrips damage leaves throughout the field via chewing and puncture-sucking damage on both leaf surfaces, and heavy feeding stress in dry weather conditions increases plant vulnerability.
